puzzles.title: Two-Space Base Extension
puzzles.concept: On 13x13, a single stone on the 3rd line makes an ideal eye-shape base by extending two spaces (skipping two intersections) along the 3rd line.
puzzles.prompt: Black has a stone at F3. Extend two spaces along the bottom side to build a solid base.

solutions.feedback: Exact! J3 is a textbook two-space extension from F3 along the 3rd line — hard to invade and quick to make two eyes.

wrongHints.G3: Too close (1-space jump) — over-concentrated on a 13x13 board.
wrongHints.K3: 3-space extension leaves a wide gap at H3 where White can wedge in.
wrongHints.default: Extend two spaces along the 3rd line from F3.

puzzles.title: Knight's Corner Enclosure (Shimari)
puzzles.concept: Two stones in a knight's move (Keima) around the 3-4 point lock down a corner and project power down the side.
puzzles.prompt: Black owns D4 (3-4 point). Form a knight's corner enclosure on the bottom side.

solutions.feedback: Clean Shimari! D4 + F3 secures the bottom-left corner and radiates influence across the bottom edge.

wrongHints.E3: A one-space jump is slower and less expansive than the knight's enclosure at F3.
wrongHints.default: Form a knight's move enclosure from D4 toward the bottom side.

puzzles.title: 3-3 Invasion Under 4-4
puzzles.concept: When an opponent leaves a 4-4 (Hoshi) stone unguarded, diving into the 3-3 point steals the corner territory cleanly.
puzzles.prompt: White's K10 stone guards the top-right loosely. Invade the 3-3 point to claim the corner.

solutions.feedback: Spot on! L11 (3-3) lives cleanly inside the corner even after White blocks at K11.

wrongHints.M12: 2-2 is too deep and gives White free thickness without extra eyes.
wrongHints.default: Aim for the 3-3 intersection directly beneath White's K10 star point.

puzzles.title: Block the 3-3 Invasion
puzzles.concept: When invaded at 3-3 under your 4-4 stone, block on the side where you have more allied stones to build a unified wall.
puzzles.prompt: White just invaded L11 under your K10 stone, and you already have support at G10. Block on the top side!

solutions.feedback: Great direction of play! Blocking at K11 connects your wall directly toward your G10 stone.

wrongHints.L10: Blocking at L10 lets White crawl out along the top edge and split K10 from G10.
wrongHints.default: Block on the top side (K11) to link with your G10 support stone.

puzzles.title: Shoulder Hit to Reduce a Moyo
puzzles.concept: Against a high 4th-line framework (moyo), a diagonal shoulder hit erases center potential while staying light and flexible.
puzzles.prompt: White has built a wide 4th-line wall at G10 and K10. Play a shoulder hit on G10 to reduce White's framework.

solutions.feedback: Textbook shoulder hit! G9 pressures G10 from the center while keeping escape paths open on both sides.

wrongHints.H10: Wedging directly between G10 and K10 on the 4th line invites a brutal double attack.
wrongHints.default: Play a diagonal shoulder hit one line below White's G10 stone.

puzzles.title: Splitting Two Enemy Extensions
puzzles.concept: When an opponent leaves a 4-space gap on a side, drop a splitting stone in the middle so they cannot link up into one giant territory.
puzzles.prompt: White has stones at D10 and J10 with a wide open gap between them. Split the top side!

solutions.feedback: Nice split! F10 divides White's two stones so each group has to make its own base separately.

wrongHints.G12: 1st-line plays surrender the entire 3rd/4th line framework to White.
wrongHints.default: Place a splitting stone right in the middle of White's D10–J10 gap on the 3rd/4th line.
